{{ElectionsNC}}
The '''2026 United States Senate election in North Carolina''' will be held on November 3, 2026, to elect a member of the [[United States Senate]] to represent the state of [[North Carolina]]. [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] former party chair [[Michael Whatley]] and [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] former governor [[Roy Cooper]] are the nominees for their respective parties. Republican incumbent [[Thom Tillis]] is not seeking a third term.

Considered vulnerable to a primary challenge due to his moderate positions, Tillis announced he would run for re-election, but withdrew after voting against the [[One Big Beautiful Bill Act]]. Whatley, who emerged as the Republican frontrunner after being endorsed by President [[Donald Trump]], won the nomination with 64.6% of the vote over author [[Don Brown (author, born 1960)|Don Brown]]. Cooper won the Democratic nomination with 92% of the vote, facing minimal opposition.

== Background ==
Democrats have not won a Senate election in North Carolina since [[2008 United States Senate election in North Carolina|2008]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/north-carolina-senate-primary-results-midterm-elections-2026/|title=Whatley, Cooper win North Carolina primaries, CBS News projects, teeing up key Senate contest|publisher=CBS News|website=CBS News|access-date=2026-10-14}}</ref>

A [[swing state]], North Carolina is considered to be a [[Red states and blue states|purple to slightly red]] Southern state at the federal level. It was also a top battleground state in the [[2020 United States presidential election in North Carolina|2020]] and [[2024 United States presidential election in North Carolina|2024]] presidential elections. The state backed [[Donald Trump]] in both elections by 1.3%<ref>{{Cite web|title=November 03, 2020 General Election Results by Contest|url=https://s3.amazonaws.com/dl.ncsbe.gov/State_Board_Meeting_Docs/2020-11-24/Canvass/State%20Composite%20Abstract%20Report%20-%20Contest.pdf|work=North Carolina State Board of Elections}}</ref> and 3.2%,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://dl.ncsbe.gov/?prefix=State_Board_Meeting_Docs/2024-11-26/Canvass/ |title=NC - State_Composite_Abstract_Report-Contest.pdf |date=November 26, 2024|access-date=December 30, 2024}}</ref> respectively.

Both parties have seen success in the state in recent years. Republicans control both chambers of the [[North Carolina General Assembly]] and hold a majority in North Carolina's [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. House]] delegation,<ref name="2024fedelection">
State Board of Elections. ''[https://er.ncsbe.gov/?election_dt=11/05/2024&county_id=0&office=FED&contest=0 General election results for Federal offices, 2024]''. North Carolina State Board of Elections. Archived at [https://web.archive.org/web/20240724000000/https://er.ncsbe.gov/?election_dt=11/05/2024&county_id=0&office=FED&contest=0 Web Archive].
</ref> as well as both of the state's U.S. Senate seats. In [[2024 North Carolina Council of State elections|2024]], Democrats won half of the state's [[North Carolina Council of State|executive offices]], flipping a net of one seat from Republicans.<ref name=2024generalncsbe>{{Cite web|url=https://er.ncsbe.gov/?election_dt=11/05/2024&county_id=0&office=COS&contest=0|title=NC SBE Contest Results|website=er.ncsbe.gov}}</ref>

==Republican primary==
Senator [[Thom Tillis]] was considered vulnerable to a primary challenger from his right. On June 10, 2023, the [[North Carolina Republican Party]] voted to censure Tillis for his support for the [[Respect for Marriage Act]] and immigration reform attempts.<ref>{{cite news |publisher=[[CNN]] |date=June 11, 2023 |url=https://www.cnn.com/2023/06/11/politics/thom-tillis-north-carolina-gop-censure/index.html |author1=Berryman, Kim |author2=Pellish, Aaron |title=Republican Sen. Thom Tillis is censured by North Carolina GOP delegates at convention}}</ref><ref name="WRALTillisSpotlight">{{cite news |title=Trump nominations put NC's Thom Tillis, the nation's 'most vulnerable' Republican senator, in the spotlight |url=https://www.wral.com/story/trump-nominations-put-nc-s-thom-tillis-the-nation-s-most-vulnerable-republican-senator-in-the-spotlight/21724608/ |access-date=November 17, 2024 |publisher=[[WRAL-TV]] |author1=Specht, Paul |author2=Doran, Will |date=November 17, 2024 |language=en}}</ref> On June 28, 2025, President [[Donald Trump]] stated he was considering backing a primary challenger after Tillis voted against a motion to consider the [[One Big Beautiful Bill Act]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=June 29, 2025 |title=Trump threatens Tillis with primary challenge |url=https://www.politico.com/live-updates/2025/06/28/congress/donald-trump-threatens-thom-tillis-00431472 |access-date=June 29, 2025 |website=[[Politico]] |author=Jacobs, Ben|language=en}}</ref> The following day, Tillis announced that he would not seek re-election.<ref name="Tillis">{{cite web|url=https://www.politico.com/news/2025/06/29/thom-tillis-retires-00432045|title=Thom Tillis says he will retire following Trump attacks|last=Carney|first=Jordain|date=June 29, 2025|access-date=June 29, 2025|website=[[Politico]]}}</ref>

==Democratic primary==

[[File:Wiley Nickel endorsing Roy Cooper for Senate.jpg|thumb|Wiley Nickel endorsing Roy Cooper for Senate]]

In 2025, Roy Cooper announced his candidacy for the United States Senate seat in the 2026 election. Shortly after his announcement, former U.S. Representative [[Wiley Nickel]], who had previously entered the race, withdrew his candidacy and endorsed Cooper for the Democratic nomination.<ref>{{cite news |last=Robertson |first=Gary D. |title=Former Congressman Wiley Nickel drops out of 2026 Senate race, endorses Roy Cooper |url=https://abc11.com/post/former-congressman-wiley-nickel-drops-2026-senate-race-endorses-north-carolina-governor-roy-cooper/17348739/
 |work=Associated Press |date=July 29, 2025}}</ref> Nickel cited Cooper's executive experience and electoral strength as reasons for his endorsement.<ref>{{cite news |title=Wiley Nickel exits North Carolina Senate race the day after Roy Cooper announces candidacy |url=https://apnews.com/article/d9da6af3c46da5a96df6c7ba5ada3ae9
 |work=Associated Press |date=July 29, 2025}}</ref>

==General election==
===Campaign===
{{expand section|date=October 2026}}
The [[Senate Leadership Fund]]—first reported by ''[[Semafor (website)|Semafor]]'' in October 2026—canceled a pledged $30 million in expenditures from Whatley's campaign to redirect support for Senator [[Roger Marshall]]'s [[2026 United States Senate election in Kansas|2026 re-election campaign in Kansas]]. Since 2025, the [[political action committee]] has spent $71 million on advertisements, largely focusing on [[Crime in North Carolina|crime and public safety]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Republicans pull funding of Trump-backed Senate candidate in critical North Carolina race|url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/oct/02/republican-pac-funding-north-carolina-senate-michael-whatley|work=[[The Guardian]]|access-date=October 2, 2026}}</ref>
